detail.hint: Drag on the chart to zoom, double-click to reset.
detail.rotating: This name answers from {n} different addresses: it is a load-balanced service. Each pass measures whichever server DNS returned, so the figures below mix machines that may sit in different places and carry different loads. A server that ignores ICMP shows up as loss.
detail.pinned: Measured at a fixed address, {ip}: the name may point elsewhere, the figures below always describe the same machine.

fed.title: Federation
fed.lead: Operators running this tool measure each other's anchors and share the results. Each pairing below was approved by a human on both sides, and is shown here only because both agreed to it.
fed.matrix_hint: Each cell is the median latency measured by the row network towards the anchor of the column network.

net.upstreams_note: Neighbours observed to the left of this network in public AS paths, ranked by visibility. Typically transit providers and large peers.
net.not_in_pdb: This network has no PeeringDB record.

about.title: About this instance
about.noc_note: To report an anomaly seen from your network, email the NOC with the permalink of the graph: it carries the target, the probe and the exact time window.
about.method_p1: Each run sends a burst of packets to the destination and keeps the full distribution of round-trip times, not an average.
about.method_p2: The median turns red and bars appear under the axis as soon as packets are lost. Percentiles stay exact at every zoom level: aggregation merges histograms rather than averaging percentiles.
about.method_p3: Measurements originate from our network. They describe the path between us and the destination, not the intrinsic quality of the destination.

pairing.title: Federation pairing
pairing.lead_open: This instance takes part in the measurement federation. Here is its identity and how to pair with it.
pairing.lead_closed: This instance has not set its AS number yet: pairing is not open.
pairing.step1: Check it against the one we gave you by phone, on an exchange mailing list or on a peering channel. If it differs, stop there.
pairing.step2: Paste this page's URL into your own back-office. Explain why you want to pair — a justification of at least {n} characters is required — and optionally add a private note for our administrator.
pairing.step3: Our administrator checks your fingerprint and your reasons, then accepts or declines, with a reply only you will see.
pairing.step4: Each side measures the other's anchors and pushes results every five minutes. The pairing is listed publicly only if both sides agreed to it.
pairing.scope_note: Only declared anchors and incidents concerning them are exchanged. On-demand measurement towards third-party prefixes is not possible, by design: it is the amplification and reconnaissance vector a probe network must refuse.
pairing.tech_body: Message-level Ed25519 signatures, 5-minute clock tolerance, replay protection by nonce cache.
